thread:
emma (support): heads up — AcmeSearch reported a spike of 5xxs on the rerank endpoint this morning after their nightly index job. p95 latency jumped and some requests hit gateway timeouts. forwarding logs.
acme_search_custrep: their internal ticket: https://acme.example/tickets/3321 — they said retrying until success, but it caused duplicate downstream work. They can repro by sending big batches of 200 candidate pairs in one rerank call.
jonah (sre): we saw a cluster-wide p95 jump from ~120ms to ~2.8s between 06:10-06:18 UTC. 504s and 502s from the gateway, lots of upstream read timeouts. error rate peaked ~6% for rerank route.
li (eng-runtime): can you paste a sample request body they used? curious about sequence lengths and batch shape.
acme_search_custrep: here's a sanitized example they sent:

```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rerank_v2",
  "queries": ["how to reset password", "reset password steps"],
  "candidates": [["doc1...long...","doc2...long..."], ... up to 200],
  "max_candidate_tokens": 1024
}
```

They said candidate docs are often large HTML blobs (~3-4k chars) and they push 150-200 candidates in single request.
emma (support): repro steps from Acme:
- send 150 candidates per query
- concurrency 40 clients in parallel
- repeated for ~2 minutes -> p95 spikes, then 502/504 starts
jonah (sre): digging into envoy/gateway logs: many requests stalled waiting for backend read. The backend reported worker pool saturation and some retry loops. We also saw increased retry attempts from the gateway making upstream timeout worse.
li (eng-runtime): hmm. Rerank execution is synchronous and tries to score each candidate; heavy candidates + large candidate count multiplies token work. Continuous batching may be creating large combined batches that overflow our per-request time SLO.
peter (product): customer expectation: rerank should handle these shapes without OOM or hitting 5xx. They flagged this as P1 because it affected production traffic.
emma (support): included metrics: (counts for the 06:10 window)
- total rerank requests: 12k
- 5xx count: 720
- p95 latency: 2800ms
- 504 gateway_timeouts: 420
jonah (sre): temporary mitigations proposed:
- throttle per-customer concurrency from their tenant to 6
- add request size/ candidate count guard at the gateway (reject >100 candidates with 413)
- short-term: increase envoy upstream timeout from 60s -> 90s? but that masks problem and can worsen queueing.
li (eng-runtime): better mitigation: add a fast-fail path when estimated token-work > X. We can compute token_est = sum(candidate_len) * num_queries and return 413 + guidance. Also consider adding streaming scoring to let smaller work finish first.
acme_search_custrep: they asked for exact limits so they can adapt client. they prefer graceful failure over opaque 502.
emma (support): told them we'll propose a safe per-request limit and a retry/backoff pattern. Also asked them to reduce concurrency for now.
li (eng-runtime): quick repro on staging: I ran a load test with 120 candidates @ avg 800 tokens candidate length, concurrency 30. I reproduced p95 ~3.1s and occasional 502s when worker queue exceeded 95%. Here's the minimal curl I used:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer test-sk" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rerank_v2","queries":["q"],"candidates":["<long html>" x 120]}'
```

Response snippet when it fails:

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{
  "error": "upstream read timeout: worker exceeded execution window"
}
```
jonah (sre): logs from the runtime node show blocking GC cycles and some slow kernel calls while copying large strings between processes. There's also evidence of retry storms from the gateway configured with 3 retries and zero jitter.
li (eng-runtime): action items I recommend (short-term):
- add per-request candidate_limit = 100 and per-request token_estimate_limit = 200k tokens (config flag)
- add queue-length based circuit breaker: when worker_queue > 80% start rejecting with 429 and Retry-After
- change gateway retry strategy to exponential backoff with jitter and reduce max_retries to 1 for 5xx on rerank
peter (product): longer term: evaluate a new rerank execution path that does chunked scoring and early stopping (stop at meaningful score delta). Also consider an alternative 'light' rerank model that is faster for high candidate counts.
emma (support): I added these recommendations to the customer's ticket and proposed the following immediate limits they can expect:
- per request max candidates: 100
- per request max candidate token sum: 200000
- per-tenant concurrent rerank requests: 6
acme_search_custrep: they accepted the temporary limits but asked for a timeline for more permanent fixes and asked if there's an SLA credit for the downtime window.
jonah (sre): we'll produce a post-incident note once we stabilize. For SLA credit — escalate to billing; need incident classification first.
li (eng-runtime): I'll ship a config gate to staging by EOD that enforces candidate_limit and a lightweight estimator to reject before scheduling. I'll also instrument a counter for `rejected_heavy_rerank` so we can measure impact.
emma (support): please ping when it's in staging so I can tell the customer. Also, can we provide a suggested client-side backoff? I suggested: full jitter backoff starting at 200ms, cap 3s, and reduce concurrency.
li (eng-runtime): ack. also note: caching doesn't help rerank much because candidates vary; but we can recommend pre-filtering client-side to drop duplicates and do cheap similarity pruning before calling rerank.
jonah (sre): follow-ups for infra:
- check if any nodes reported OOMs during window
- confirm gateway retry config and add jitter
- add an alert for worker_queue > 75% persisting for >1m
emma (support): thanks everyone. I'll update Acme's ticket with the short-term limits and the staging deployment ETA. Keeping thread open for EE/prod verification.
